IEAGHG (M. Garcia, N. Berghout, L. Herraiz), "Cost of CO2 Capture in the Industrial Sector: Cement and Iron and Steel Industries", IEAGHG Technical Review 2018-TR03, IEA Greenhouse Gas R&D Programme, Cheltenham, September 2018. www.ieaghg.org. No DOI printed.

This is a literature review that standardises published cases to North-West Europe ($2016, 8% real discount rate, 25-yr life, 80% CF). LOADED: (a) the report's own results, Table 10 BASIS scenario, as ten technology groups (cement: traditional amine, advanced amine, membranes, oxyfuel, solids-based, hybrid; iron and steel: traditional amine, advanced amine, VPSA, hybrid TGROBF): CO2 avoidance cost (abatement-cost) and CO2 capture cost (cost-levelized, per t captured) as min/max ranges, plus the standardised discount rate and capacity factor; (b) Tables 1 and 2, the per-case inputs of the underlying studies, marked "reprinted from": capture rate, capital cost as printed in original currency/year and cost basis (TCR/TPC/TIC/spent/unstated; not standardised; capacity of each case not printed), positive electricity use (GJ/t CO2), and fuel use where the case detail names gas as the energy source. NOT LOADED (in _other-values.csv): no-heat-recovery and no-electricity-export scenario ranges, increase of manufacturing cost per t cement/steel, negative (export) electricity values, fuel use with unstated carrier, the implausible steam entry, and general assumptions (prices, plant sizes, cost factors, regeneration energies). NOT TRANSCRIBED: the per-case standardised bar-chart values in Figures 7-12 and 18-23 (cost breakdown per t CO2 avoided and per t product, specific CO2 avoided); the steel figures are only partly legible in the text layer and the cement figures are images, so no reliable case-to-number assignment was possible. The report gives no standardised capex, O&M, CO2 captured per year or capture-plant energy per case, so no capacity, capex (own results) or opex rows exist for the Table 10 groups.

(1) Standardised capacity factor: Table 8 gives 80% for cement, Section 5.2.1 says the cement comparison uses 85%.; (2) Cover dates the report September 2018 while every page footer says August 2018.; (3) Summary text (p.59) gives 79-180 $/t avoided for traditional chemical absorption in cement while Table 10 and the executive summary give 72-180; p.44 gives 72-199 for amine-based PCC.; (4) Executive summary (p.1) gives 56-93 $/t avoided for chemical absorption across steelmaking routes, while Table 10 (basis) gives 56-82 for traditional absorption.; (5) Table 10 footnote f: the no-electricity-export scenario gives lower costs than the basis for steel chemical absorption, a stated artefact of the method.; (6) Tables 1 and 2 mix cost bases (TCR, TPC, TIC, total spent, "Capex", "investment cost", unstated) and currencies/years (M EUR 2012-2014, M USD 2007-2012), and do not state whether new-construction figures cover the capture plant only; Ho et al. (2013) basis unknown (p.30).; (7) Table 2 Ozcan hybrid electricity printed "0..79"; Anantharaman steam "6-9 *10E-5" GJ/t is implausible; indirect calcination electricity "From -0.2 to 0.8".; (8) Table 1 energy columns are headed GJ/tCO2 without saying captured or avoided; fuel carrier not named.; (9) Footnote 9 gives solvent make-up in "Kg/t CO2" and regeneration energy in MJ/kg; text p.30 says heat of absorption "between 3.2 and 4 MJ/tCO2 captured" (should be MJ/kg or GJ/t).; (10) Glossary defines MEA as "Monoethylethanolamine" and MDEA as "Monodiethylethanolamine".; (11) Section 3.4.3 refers to "Equations 14 + 15" for equipment-cost standardisation (Table 5) but these equations are numbered 11 and 12; scenario C boiler cost 85 EUR/kW has no price year.; (12) Section 5.2.2 refers to Figure 26, which does not exist (Figure 22).; (13) Tsupari et al. is cited as both 2013 and 2015 for the same cases in text and figures; Tsupari 2013 is missing from the reference list.
